en.headline: Runners criticise inaugural Northern Metropolis Marathon arrangements
en.dek: Participants reported water shortages, hot conditions, uneven terrain and a long post-race walk after the event drew about 15,000 runners on Sunday.
body: Runners have raised concerns about the inaugural Northern Metropolis Marathon held on Sunday, citing water shortages, hot conditions, uneven terrain and a lengthy walk to collect belongings after finishing.

The event, organised by the New Territories Heung Yee Kuk to mark its 100th anniversary, attracted about 15,000 registered participants across full marathon, half marathon, 10km and shorter races. Organisers had presented it as a showcase for development in the Northern Metropolis.

Experts said the issues went beyond ordinary first-time problems and urged organisers to ensure professional expertise for any future editions. The route included sections of the newly opened Fanling Bypass and the Lung Shan Tunnel.
No official response from the organisers to the specific complaints was detailed in reports on Tuesday.

zh.headline: 跑手批評首屆北部都會區馬拉松安排
zh.dek: 約1.5萬名跑手周日參賽後，反映缺水、天氣炎熱、路況不平及賽後取回物品需長途步行。
body: 跑手對周日舉行的首屆北部都會區馬拉松提出批評，指比賽期間出現缺水、天氣炎熱、路況不平，以及完賽後需長途步行取回物品等問題。
賽事由新界鄉議局主辦，以慶祝成立100周年，吸引約1.5萬名報名者參加全馬、半馬、10公里及其他較短距離賽事。主辦方曾將活動定位為展示北部都會區發展的平台。
專家表示，問題超出首次舉辦常見的起步問題，呼籲主辦方若再辦類似賽事，須確保具備專業經驗。路線包括新開通的粉嶺繞道及龍山隧道部分路段。
周二報道未有詳述主辦方對具體投訴的正式回應。
